records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:31 — rss.items.each loop has no per-item rescue, so one bad item (import error, malformed content) aborts processing of all remaining feed items for that hour with no retry
records.rationale: The diff shows poll_feed iterating rss.items with no rescue around the per-item processing (content parsing, TopicEmbed.import), and the job sets `sidekiq_options retry: false`. So an exception on any item (e.g. CGI.unescapeHTML, scrub, or import failure) aborts the loop and skips all remaining items for that hourly run, with no retry. Mechanism is verifiable in the new code.

records.issue_text: app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb:33 — Same line-anchored regex bypass (url !~ /^https?\:\/\//) used to validate RSS item link/id; zero coverage for malformed or multiline feed URLs designed to bypass it
records.rationale: The regex in poll_feed.rb is `url !~ /^https?\:\/\//` and it falls back to `i.id` when the link is blank or non-http — it is not described in the diff as a security boundary being bypassed, but more importantly the finding claims a 'regex bypass' with 'zero coverage for malformed or multiline feed URLs'. In the diff, non-matching URLs cause fallback to `i.id` (or nil), and the actual gate is TopicEmbed.import's `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which rejects non-http URLs — so malformed/non-http feed URLs are dropped, not imported. A multiline URL would fail the anchored regex in TopicEm

records.issue_text: app/models/topic_embed.rb:11 — url =~ /^https?\:\/\// uses Ruby's line-anchored ^/$, which match per-line not whole-string, so a crafted multiline url (e.g. "javascript:x\nhttp://evil") bypasses the scheme check; no test covers this
records.rationale: The regex `/^https?\:\/\//` in TopicEmbed.import uses line-anchored ^, which matches on any line of a multiline string, so a url like "x\nhttp://evil" passes the scheme check. The mechanism is real and the url flows in from external input (params[:embed_url] via embed controller → RetrieveTopic → TopicRetriever → TopicEmbed.import_remote/import). Whether a fully exploitable path exists depends on downstream URI parsing, so confidence is moderate.

records.issue_text: lib/topic_retriever.rb:41 — perform_retrieve directly instantiates and synchronously runs Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({}), coupling a plain library class to a scheduled job's internals instead of a shared abstraction
records.rationale: The diff shows lib/topic_retriever.rb perform_retrieve calling 'Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})' synchronously inside a plain library class, which couples TopicRetriever to a scheduled job's internals and re-runs an hourly feed poll inline during a request-triggered retrieve. This is a real, specific architectural/coupling concern grounded in the diff, not a defect or style nit.
